newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Mandela to meet UNITA leader on Monday.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mandela to meet UNITA leader on Monday.

text.p: Angolan opposition leader Jonas Savimbi will travel to South Africa on Monday to meet President Nelson Mandela ahead of the formation of Angola's first unity government, a spokesman said.

Savimbi, who will meet Mandela in an official capacity for the first time since South Africa's historic all-race polls in 1994, is to see him at his holiday home in the rural Qunu district, presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana confirmed.
"The meeting will be on Monday. Savimbi and President (Jose Eduardo) dos Santos are in constant contact with the president and this meeting takes place in that context," Mankahlana told Reuters.

He said Savimbi, leader of the UNITA (National Union for the Total Indedependence of Angola) party, was expected to brief Mandela on the latest developments in the Angolan peace process. Mandela planned to announce his attendance at the inauguration of Angola's new government in Luanda later this month, Mankahlana said.
Angola's two rival groups agreed last month to form a government of national reconciliation on January 23 in a landmark move on the country's path to peace after nearly two decades of civil war.
UNITA and the dos Santos government signed a peace pact in November 1994. About 7,000 United Nations peacekeeping troops have been monitoring implementation of the pact's provisions.
